thread:
anya: quick flag — onboarding lumen-lite-v2 shows a recall@1 drop for short queries (<=8 tokens) on our holdout. baseline recall@1=0.62, lumen-lite-v2=int8 recall@1=0.50. ran microbatch sims, looks consistent. anyone have immediate ideas?
ravi: ouch, that's large. Is this across languages or just en?
anya: looks primarily english short queries. multilang k=1 drop smaller (around 4%).
jordan: can you paste the eval snippet and k-values? also was this quantized per-channel or symmetric?
anya: eval snippet:
```
python eval.py --model lumen-lite-v2 --quant int8_per_channel --holdout holdout_10k_short.json --metrics recall@1,5
```
metrics summary:
```
baseline_fp16 recall@1 0.62 recall@5 0.81
lumen-lite-v2_int8 recall@1 0.50 recall@5 0.78
```
luis: interesting — recall@5 drop is small but r@1 big. suggests top-neighbor ordering shuffled. maybe nearest neighbor distance compression on short vectors. can you share embedding length distribution for short queries vs baseline?
anya: embed norms mean:
```
baseline_fp16 mean_norm 1.02 std 0.12
lumen-lite-v2_int8 mean_norm 0.91 std 0.21
```
maria: increased variance could cause nearest-neighbor instability. did you run whitening/centering postproc like they do in baseline pipeline?
anya: yes same pipeline: l2norm then PCA-whiten using the baseline's PCA fit.
jordan: what about kvcache or batching differences during inference? short sequences can have different attention patterns affecting representation.
anya: this was offline eval from stored embeddings (no runtime kv), so not runtime effect.
luis: could be quantization aliasing: check layernorm scale/clamp differences. run a per-dim KS test between fp16 and int8 embeddings on shortholdout.
anya: running now, will post results.
(2m later)
anya: KS per-dim top outliers: dims 27, 89, 112 show p<1e-6. also a small set of dims drift mean by >0.12.
ravi: could try hybrid quant: int8 for dense layers but keep layernorm fp16 or int16. quick AB?
maria: also try evaluating centroid stability: compute cluster assignments (kmeans k=10) and see class flip rates between versions.
anya: ran quick kmeans: flip rate ~14% for short queries, baseline vs lumen-int8.
jordan: that matches r@1 drop. action items:
- anya: run per-layer activation histograms and try int8-per-channel vs int8-symmetric (deadline EOD)
- luis: prototype keeping layernorm in fp16 and re-eval
- maria: compute centroid flip map + silhouette for shortholdout
- ravi: sanity run with fp16 lumen-lite-v2 to check model arch regression
ops-bot: scheduled ephemeral job eval-4678901234 on prod-batch-3, ETA 30m :gear:
anya: thanks — will update here. if anyone sees faster probe to isolate, ping me.
